issues.legal_issue: A company court cannot supervise or fetter a secured creditor’s enforcement and sale of secured assets under the securitisation statute merely because the borrower company is in liquidation.
material_facts: The secured creditor had assigned its rights to a reconstruction company, which elected to remain outside the winding-up proceedings and enforce the security under the securitisation statute.

The company court permitted that enforcement but required the reconstruction company to submit sale proposals and valuations to the Official Liquidator, advertise the winding-up proceedings, account for its claim and expenses, and deposit any surplus with the Official Liquidator.

The securitisation statute and its rules provide for notice to the borrower at relevant stages; where the borrower is a company in liquidation, the Official Liquidator represents it and can seek information about workmen’s dues and challenge the secured creditor’s steps through the statutory appeal process.
The statute provides for distribution of sale proceeds in accordance with workmen’s rights and priorities, including depositing workmen’s dues with the liquidator.
issues.conclusion: A secured creditor that elects to remain outside the winding up may enforce and sell its security under the securitisation statute without supervisory directions or other fetters imposed by the company court or Official Liquidator. The liquidator is to be associated as the borrower’s representative for the statutory protections of workmen and may use the statutory appeal process; the completed sale in the lead matter was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 9 and 13 of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, particularly Section 13(9) and its provisos, establish a self-contained process for enforcing security without court or tribunal intervention and protect workmen’s dues by incorporating the relevant safeguards of Sections 529 and 529A of the Companies Act, 1956. Sections 17 and 18 of the 2002 Act provide remedies to the borrower, represented in liquidation by the Official Liquidator; Rules 8 and 9 of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 provide for notices in the enforcement and sale process. The Court distinguished the earlier authorities concerning the State Financial Corporations Act and the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, including Rajasthan State Financial Corporation v. Official Liquidator, Allahabad Bank v. Canara Bank, and Bank of Maharashtra v. Pandurang Keshav Gorwardkar, because the securitisation statute itself provides for enforcement, workmen’s protections, and remedies. It also referred to Mardia Chemicals v. Union of India and to Sections 35 and 37 of the 2002 Act.

rule.if: secured_enforcement_proceeding and borrower_company_in_liquidation and creditor_elects_outside_winding_up and statutory_workmen_safeguards_exist

predicates.secured_enforcement_proceeding: A secured creditor or its assignee undertakes to enforce and sell secured assets under a statutory process that authorizes enforcement without court or tribunal intervention.
predicates.borrower_company_in_liquidation: The borrower whose assets are secured is a company in liquidation or winding up.
predicates.creditor_elects_outside_winding_up: The secured creditor elects to enforce its security outside the winding-up process.
predicates.statutory_workmen_safeguards_exist: The enforcement framework gives the liquidator notice and a role in protecting workmen’s dues, provides for their priority in distribution of proceeds, and allows statutory review of enforcement steps.

issues.definition: When a secured creditor enforces security outside the winding up of a company and the enforcement framework protects workmen and provides review, the company court cannot fetter that enforcement.

issues.legal_issue: A confirmed auction sale conducted fairly at an adequate price is not ordinarily reopened merely because a higher offer is made later.
material_facts: The company court confirmed the sale after a competitive process that included an open bid, further advertisement, and no offer exceeding the accepted bid during that process.
The accepted price was found to be fair in light of valuation material and the competitive sale process.
No illegality, irregularity, fraud, or collusion in the auction was established.
A later higher offer was made after confirmation of the sale.
issues.conclusion: The confirmed sale was not set aside, and the appeals challenging it were dismissed; the later higher offer did not by itself justify disturbing the sale.
issues.legal_principle: Under Valji Khimji & Co. v. Official Liquidator of Hindustan Nitro Product (Gujarat) Ltd., a later higher offer does not ordinarily justify setting aside a confirmed sale after an adequately publicized auction, though a grossly inadequate sale price may support an inference of fraud or collusion. Vedica Procon Private Limited v. Balleshwar Greens P. Ltd. approved the principle in Navalkha and Sons v. Sri Ramanya Das that a company court may accept or reject a bid before confirmation, but once satisfied that the price is adequate, a subsequent higher offer is not a ground to refuse confirmation.

rule.if: confirmed_auction_sale_appeal and sale_was_fairly_publicized and competitive_sale_was_fair and accepted_price_was_adequate and no_sale_misconduct_established and later_higher_offer_only

predicates.confirmed_auction_sale_appeal: A party challenges an order confirming an auction sale.
predicates.sale_was_fairly_publicized: The sale was advertised in a manner that gave eligible bidders a fair opportunity to participate.
predicates.competitive_sale_was_fair: The auction or bidding process was conducted competitively and fairly.
predicates.accepted_price_was_adequate: The court found the accepted price adequate in light of the sale process and relevant valuation material.
predicates.no_sale_misconduct_established: No fraud, collusion, illegality, or material irregularity in the sale was established.
predicates.later_higher_offer_only: A higher offer was made after confirmation, without other established grounds that undermine the sale.

issues.definition: A confirmed sale reached through a fair, adequately publicized process at an adequate price is not reopened solely because a higher offer arrives later.

issues.legal_issue: An entity that is neither a secured creditor of the company nor the successor to its secured creditor cannot require association in the secured creditor’s sale process on that basis.
material_facts: The entity had paid liabilities owed to three banks as guarantor and acquired a charge only over the company’s movable raw materials.
The secured creditor enforcing the security was a different creditor, and the entity had neither become that creditor’s successor nor established itself as a secured creditor of the company.
The entity sought to be associated with the sale process and challenged the secured creditor’s permission to remain outside the winding up.
issues.conclusion: The entity had no basis to require association in the sale process or to prevent the secured creditor from remaining outside the winding up; its appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held on the facts that the entity was neither a secured creditor of the company nor a successor to the secured creditor whose security was being enforced. Its guarantor payments and charge over different movable assets did not give it a right to participate in enforcement of the other creditor’s security under the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002.

predicates.challenge_to_creditor_electing_outside_w: An entity challenges a secured creditor’s election to enforce its security outside the company’s winding-up process or seeks participation in that creditor’s sale.
predicates.challenger_is_not_secured_creditor: The challenging entity does not hold the security being enforced and is not otherwise a secured creditor of the company in respect of that security.
predicates.challenger_is_not_successor_to_secured_c: The challenging entity has not succeeded to the rights of the secured creditor whose security is being enforced.

issues.definition: An entity that challenges a secured creditor’s separate enforcement but holds neither that security nor successor rights cannot require participation in that creditor’s sale.
